questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for some administrative processes to take time, especially course registration and changes to your Learning Agreement. It is a good idea to arrive with some flexibility and contact the international office early if anything is unclear.

Check the language of instruction for each course carefully. Courses can be taught in Spanish, Catalan or sometimes English, so make sure you know the teaching language before finalising your course selection.

Take advantage of both the university and the city. Barcelona is a great place to study abroad, so I would recommend joining activities, meeting both local and international students, and exploring the city and Catalonia alongside your studies.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange was experiencing a new academic and cultural environment while becoming more independent. Studying in Barcelona gave me the opportunity to improve my Spanish, meet people from different countries, and gain new perspectives both academically and personally. I also really appreciated being able to experience the city and local culture as part of my everyday life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was navigating the administrative side of the exchange, especially course registration, documentation and making sure everything was approved correctly between the host university and UCPH. It could sometimes be confusing and time-consuming, but it also taught me to be more proactive, organised and independent.
